case_title: Ram Pal @ Bunda v. State of Haryana
accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity/dispute: the accused had an inimical relationship with the victim's family, stemming from his earlier misbehaviour towards the victim's elder sister and a village panchayat apology; no direct relationship with the victim is described
weapon: Not stated as a weapon; the victim's neck was wrapped with a blue shawl owned by her, and death was by strangulation
evidence_type: Circumstantial, with medical (post-mortem and forensic) evidence, motive evidence and eyewitness-type testimony of presence at the scene
aggravating_circumstances: Rape and murder of the victim; death by strangulation with contusions on face and chin and abrasions on back
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC ss.302 and 376; sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for life and 10 years rigorous imprisonment
high_court_outcome: Appeal (Criminal Appeal No. 686-DB of 2006) dismissed; conviction and sentence confirmed
neutral_facts: On 18 February 2005 at about 6:30 p.m. the victim went to fields near her village to ease herself and did not return. Her family searched but could not find her. During the search the accused was found in the fields. When the victim's mother asked him where her daughter was, he did not respond and ran away from the place. He could not be traced in the village until 21 February 2005, when he was reportedly produced and arrested. The victim's body was found the next morning in daylight in fields belonging to another person, with her neck wrapped in a blue shawl that belonged to her. The family had earlier had a dispute with the accused: some years before, he and a cousin had teased the victim's elder sister on a path, the matter was taken to a village panchayat, and both apologised; the accused was said to have later threatened revenge. Medical examination showed death by asphyxia due to strangulation, ante-mortem and sufficient to cause death. There were multiple abrasions and contusions on the face, chin and back. Forensic examination found blood on the shawl, salwar and underwear of the victim. Human semen was detected on a vaginal swab from the victim. The accused's underwear, taken on his examination after arrest, also showed human semen. The medical evidence indicated the victim had been subjected to sexual intercourse before her death.
physical_harm: Death by asphyxia due to strangulation; multiple abrasions and contusions on face and chin; superficial abrasions on back; victim subjected to sexual intercourse before death
motive: Revenge for the accused's humiliation at the village panchayat over his earlier misconduct (teasing the victim's elder sister in 2002) and the apology he was forced to give
key_evidence_accepted: Medical evidence of death by strangulation and sexual intercourse before death; FSL reports of blood and semen on victim's clothing and vaginal swab and semen on accused's underwear; PW-10's evidence that the accused was present at the scene and ran away; PW-12's evidence of the accused's absence for two days; PW-11's motive evidence, corroborated by PW-10
witness_credibility: PW-10's evidence on the accused's presence at the scene was accepted despite minor variations from her police statement; PW-11's motive evidence was corroborated by PW-10; PW-12's evidence on absence was accepted as the record was not contradicted, despite PW-13 turning hostile
post_offence_conduct: Ran away from the scene without answering the mother's questions and remained absconding for two days; found absent from the village until arrest on 21.2.2005
trial_duration: offence: 18.2.2005; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 07.09.2011; Supreme Court: 11 April 2013
legal_representation: Appellant (accused): R.K. Talwar, David Rao, K. Kaushik, Chander Shekhar Ashri; Respondent (State of Haryana): Kamal Mohan Gupta
investigation_status: Body found after police intimation; accused arrested on 21.2.2005; forensic and medical reports obtained; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under ss.302 and 376 IPC, life imprisonment and 10 years RI; High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction and sentence confirmed; Supreme Court: appeal dismissed
legal_principle_applied: Circumstantial evidence: the proved circumstances must form a complete chain with no missing link pointing to the accused; motive and conduct considered alongside medical evidence
